title: Stock Market Update: Stocks Rebound, S&P Nearly Flat for the Week

organizations.name: real estate moving the market stocks

text:
Strong: Technology, Utilities, Communication Services Weak: Financials, Energy, Materials, Consumer Staples, Real Estate Moving the Market
Stocks extend gains on reports that China is open to further trade talks with the U.S.
Investors continue to digest yesterday's policy statement from the Fed
Apple (AAPL) outperforms after being initiated with an 'Overweight' rating at JPMorgan Stocks Rebound, S&P Nearly Flat for the Week 27-Sep-18 12:55 ET Dow +167.17 at 26552.45, Nasdaq +81.17 at 8071.52, S&P +21.23 at 2927.20
[BRIEFING.COM] The stock market has rebounded following yesterday's late sell off, and is currently at session highs following reports that China is open to further trade talks with the United States. The S&P 500 is up 0.7%, trimming its weekly loss to 0.1%, while the Dow and the Nasdaq sport gains of 0.6% and 1.0%, respectively.
Investors are continuing to digest Wednesday's policy statement from the Fed, which included a rate hike and the removal of the word 'accomodative', leading some to believe that the Fed might be adjusting its thinking on monetary policy. However, Fed Chairman Jerome Powell later said that the language change does not signal a change in the Fed's path for rate hikes.
10 of the 11 S&P sectors are in positive territory this afternoon, with utilities (+1.3%) and communications services (+1.3%) leading the charge. Within the communication space, FAANG names Alphabet (GOOG 1201.28, +20.79) and Facebook (FB 170.96, +4.02) are outperforming with gains of 1.8% and 2.4%, respectively.
Meanwhile, in the information technology space (+0.8%), the S&P 500's largest company by market cap, Apple (AAPL 225.65, +5.23), is outperforming after being initiated with an 'Overweight' rating at JPMorgan Chase. Apple shares are currently higher by 2.3%.
The lightly-weighted materials sector is the only group in the red, showing a loss of 0.6%.
In earnings news, shares of Bed Bath & Beyond (BBBY 14.69, -4.12) have plunged 21.9%, hitting their lowest level in nearly two decades, after the company missed Q2 earnings estimates. Same-store sales declined for the sixth straight quarter, dropping 0.6%, and the company issued below-consensus guidance for FY19.
Accenture (ACN 170.55, -2.42, -1.4%), Carnival (CCL 63.73, -3.25, -4.9%), McCormick (MKC 128.85, -1.04, -0.8%), Conagra (CAG 33.81, -2.26, -6.3%), and Rite Aid (RAD 1.27, -0.01, -0.8%) are also down after reporting their quarterly results.
In Washington, Christine Ford, who has accused President Trump's Supreme Court nominee Brett Kavanaugh of sexually assaulting her back in high school, testified before the Senate Judiciary Committee this morning. Judge Kavanaugh, who has denied the allegations, is up next.
Investors received a big batch of economic data today that included Durable Goods Orders for August, the third estimate for Q2 GDP, weekly Initial Claims, advance readings for August International Trade in Goods, Retail Inventories, and Wholesale Inventories, and the Pending Home Sales report for August: August durable goods orders rose 4.5% (Briefing.com consensus +1.8%), and the prior month's reading was revised to -1.2% (from -1.7%). Excluding transportation, durable orders increased 0.1% (Briefing.com consensus +0.4%) to follow the prior month's unrevised reading of +0.2%. The key takeaway from the report is that the headline increase was driven by a jump in nondefense aircraft and parts orders while growth in other areas was shy of expectations. The third estimate of second quarter GDP pointed to an expansion of 4.2% (Briefing.com consensus 4.3%), unchanged from the second estimate. The key takeaway from the report is that it showed no change in personal spending growth (3.8%) from the second estimate. The latest weekly initial jobless claims count totaled 214,000, while the Briefing.com consensus expected a reading of 209,000. Today's tally was above the revised prior week count of 202,000 (from 201,000). As for continuing claims, they rose to 1.661 million from an unrevised count of 1.645 million. The key takeaway from the report is that even with the increase in initial and continuing claims, both series remain near their lowest levels in almost 50 years. The Advance report for International Trade in Goods for August showed a deficit of $75.8 billion (Briefing.com consensus -$71.0 billion). Meanwhile, the Advance report for Wholesale Inventories for August showed an increase of 0.8%, and the Advance report for Retail Inventories for August showed an increase of 0.7%. Pending Home Sales decreased 1.8% in August (Briefing.com consensus -0.4%). Today's reading follows a revised 0.8% decrease in July (from -0.7%). Add this to my Page Alerts . MARKET PLACE
